questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick the option that gives their correct order.

A. These tribes believe that they can communicate with dead ancestors only through this language.

B. Today, linguists call such a language an “isolated” language.

C. Zuni is a language spoken only by the Zuni tribes.

D. It is remarkable that these tribes have been able to preserve their language.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2.**

**First is C **as it introduces the subject i.e Zuni.

**Next is A** as it further explains what the tribes believe.

**After that is D** as it describes how these tribes have preserved the language.

**Last is B** as it highlights the present scenario.

**The correct sequence is -CADB.**

questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate option to change the narration (direct / indirect) of the given sentence.

Mary said, “I have to be there by 10 am tomorrow.”

options.text: Mary is telling me that she has to be there by 10 am tomorrow
Mary says to me that she has to be there by 10 am.
Mary told me that she had to be there by 10 am the next day.
Mary tells me she has to be there by 10 am tomorrow.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 3.**

The speaker is **informing** something i.e **told** will be used.

**Tomorrow **will be changed to **the next day** in indirect speech.

**The first person** pronoun will be changed **to the third person** i.e. she.

Also, the **past participle** form of the verb will be used.

So option 3 is correct.

questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate option to change the voice (active / passive) form of the given sentence.

I am writing a story after a long time.

options.text: A story is being written by me after a long time.
I have written a story after a long time.
A story after a long time was written by me.
A story had been written by me after a long time.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1.**

In the **passive voice**, the **subject and the object get interchanged.** The **subject** will become **a story**.

The sentence is in the** present continuous tense. **

So, the **passive voice** will be of the form **passive subject+is/are being+past participle form of verb+passive object**.

So, option 1 is correct.

questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate option to change the narration (direct / indirect) of the given sentence.

Sumit said, “I will be leaving for London this summer so I can meet you only when I return.”

options.text: Sumit said that he would be leaving for London that summer and he could meet me only when he returned.
Sumit said he will go to London this summer and he would meet me only when he will be returning.
Sumit said he will be leaving for London this summer and he could meet him only when he returned.
Sumit said he will have gone to London that summer and could meet me only when he returned.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1.**

In the indirect form, **will** changes to **would** and **can **changes to **could**.

Also, **the first person** changes to the **third person**.

So,** I **will change to **he** and **you** will change to **me.**

Also, the **base form** of the verb will be changed to **past participle** form i.e **returned**. So, option 1 is correct.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom (in the context) to fill in the sentence.

Pallavi worked really hard for the examination and ______ to gain success.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"left no stone unturned". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Left no stone unturned: **This idiom means to try every possible course of action in order to achieve something.
 
• It suggests that Pallavi worked exhaustively, trying every possible method to do well in the exam.
 
• It's a good fit for the sentence.
 
• So, the complete sentence would be: 
 
 
• "Pallavi worked really hard for the examination and left no stone unturned to gain success."
 
• This sentence conveys the idea that Pallavi made every possible effort to succeed in the examination.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 1". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Hit the bull’s eye:
 
 
• It generally means achieving an objective precisely.
 
• However, this idiom is more often used to describe the accomplishment itself rather than the effort put in to achieve something - here, the sentence is describing the effort more than the result.
 
 
 
• Beat about the bush:
 
 
• This idiom means to avoid getting to the point.
 
• It wouldn't be a fitting idiom in this context since it doesn't express hard work or effort.
 
 
 
• Struck a sour note:
 
 
• This phrase typically refers to doing something that spoils an otherwise pleasant situation or event.
 
• It does not reflect hard work to achieve success and is not appropriate for this sentence context.
